title: Unemployment Insurance Appeals: Video Hearing Sessions Booked by a Party
content:
**Unemployment Insurance Appeals — hearing by video.** Dockets with hearings are set for a hearing in the docket's default mode, and a party may ask for an in-person hearing where the docket allows it or for a video hearing on any docket that holds hearings; the Board of Review decides on the record and sets no hearing, accepting written argument within its written argument days. A party who asks for a video hearing books the video session itself on the Department's video hearing calendar, and the session replaces the telephone setting on the appeal as a change of hearing mode made at that party's request.

## Not a postponement

A party may ask to postpone a set hearing, and the postponement rules, with their lead time, per-party maximum and reschedule window, govern that request; a party's request to hold its set hearing as a video session instead is a change of hearing mode and is not a request to postpone. A change of hearing mode booked as a video session is not a postponement: it needs no postponement request or decision, is not subject to the postponement lead time, does not count toward the party's postponements and is not held to the reschedule window; its date is the video session date.

## Status of the appeal

A video session is booked only for an appeal that stands at filed or scheduled status. On an appeal at filed status, a video session is booked only after the appeal stands at scheduled status with its first hearing setting on record.

| Status shown on the appeal record | Video session |
|---|---|
| scheduled | meets the status condition |
| filed | not booked while the appeal stands at filed status; booked only once the appeal stands at scheduled status with its first hearing setting on record |
| dismissed, decided, withdrawn or closed | not booked |

The result governed here is the video session date, expressed as the video session notice period: the whole number of calendar days from today, the day the party books the session and its notice is mailed, to the video session date.

## The tool: `book_video_hearing_session_16bf8e4f`

**Owner and how it is invoked.** A customer-side tool. The agent unlocks `book_video_hearing_session_16bf8e4f` and hands it over; the customer themselves — the party who asked for the video hearing — runs it to book the session.

**What one call does.** It records a new hearing setting on the appeal in video mode at 13:00 local time, with its notice mailed today, entered as a change of hearing mode made at the party's request (not a postponement, so no postponement reason is recorded), and it moves the appeal's hearing date to the video session date. The party sees the video session date on the appeal and in its activity history; the earlier telephone date is no longer the hearing date.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `appeal_id` | the docket number of the party's appeal, as the agent reads it to the party from the appeal record before booking | identifier text |
| `session_days` | the whole number of calendar days from today's date (counted as day 0) to the video session date; the figure is given to the party by the agent | an integer; the tool records the session as the YYYY-MM-DD date that many calendar days after today |

**Return.** A text receipt of a dictionary with: `appeal_id` (the docket number), `appeal_event_id` (the reference number of the video-session setting), `hearing_date` (the video session date, YYYY-MM-DD), `hearing_time` ("13:00"), `hearing_mode` ("video") and `notice_mailed_date` (today's date, YYYY-MM-DD). The call has succeeded when the receipt shows `hearing_mode` video and the new hearing date.

*Input and receipt (hypothetical):* booked on 15 April 2026 with `session_days` 26, the receipt shows `hearing_date` "2026-05-11", `hearing_time` "13:00" and `hearing_mode` "video".
